english.html: tainted and convicted: but only to speak of the penalty, in which the old Romans do not show themselves severe, inasmuch as in those times there were no lurkers after other men's marriages, and one did not hear tell of immodesties nor lecheries <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>; which was the reason also for which Lycurgus in Lacedaemon established no penalties at all against adulterers <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>. As to our Jurisconsults: it seems to many that they did not make the penalty of this crime capital <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>, nay, that they did not wish to punish it with a simple banishment, unless when the adultery was joined with incest, as if one had abused a married kinswoman of one's own <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>. Nevertheless our Emperors, especially the Christian and Catholic ones, after the example of the Law of God (by which adulterers must die <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>), have holily judged this crime not only capital, but, passing yet further, worthy of the sword and of natural death <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>. Among whom Opilius Macrinus, the twenty-third Emperor, had the two bodies of the adulterous man and woman tied together and burnt alive together <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>; nay, one day he had two of his soldiers (who had violated a woman) put into the bellies of two oxen, each into his own, and their bodies there sewn up and enclosed entirely, except the head, which showed, so that they might be seen speaking together and deploring their misery <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. But yet, weighing well the texts of our Jurisconsults, whatever may have been thought until now, they have done no less; which our Justinian shows expressly, when he says that the Julian law on adulterers (interpreted by the Jurisconsults in the Pandects) punished with the sword, that is to say with death, those who thus profane and violate marriages <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>. It is true that for the quality of the persons, or other circumstances, sometimes this penalty of the sword and of natural death has been restrained and moderated to banishment or other civil death <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>. lines: taint & conuaincu: mais ſeulement parler de la peine
en laquelle les vieux Romains ne ſe monſtrent pas ſe-
ueres, pourautant qu'en ce temps là ny auoit point au
cuns guetteurs de mariages d'autruy, & n'entendoit-on
parler d'impudicitez, ni paillardiſes {a}; qui fut la raiſon
auſſi, pour laquelle Lycurgus en Lacedemone, ne con-
ſtitua peines aucunes contre les adulteres {b}. Touchant
nos Iuriſconſultes. Il ſemble à pluſieurs qu'ils n'ayent
point fait la peine de ce crime capitale {c}: voire que ne
l'ayent voulu punir d'vn ſimple banniſſement: ſi ce n'eſt
quand l'adultere eſtoit conioint auec inceſte: comme
ſi on auoit abuſé d'vne ſienne parente mariee {d}. Tou-
tesfois nos Empereurs, meſmement les Chreſtiens, &
Catholiques, à l'exemple de la Loy de Dieu (par la-
quelle les adulteres doyuent mourir {e}) ont ſainctemẽt:
iugé ce crime, non ſeulement capital: mais paſſant en-
core plus outre, digne du glaiue, & de mort naturelle {f}.
Entre leſquels, Opilius Macrinus xxiij Empereur fai-
ſoit attacher les deux corps de l'homme & de la fem
me adulteres, & bruſler enſemblemẽt tous vifs {g} voire
vn iour fit mettre deux ſiens ſoldars (qui auoient vio-
lé vne femme) dans le ventre de deux bœufs, chacun
dans le ſien, & illec coudre & enclorre leurs corps
entierement: reſerué la teſte qui ſe monſtroit, à fin
qu'on les peuſt voir parler enſemble, & deplorer leur
miſere {h}. Mais encor, à bien poiſer les textes de nos
Iuriſconſultes, quoy que l'on ayt penſé iuſques icy, ils
n'en ont pas moins fait. ce que noſtre Iuſtinien mon-
ſtre diſertement, quand il dit que la loy Iulie, des adul-
teres (interpretée par les Iuriſconſultes aux Pande-
ctes) a puni du glaiue, c'eſt à dire de mort, ceux qui pro
fanent & violent ainſi les mariages {i}. Il eſt vray que
pour la qualité des perſonnes, ou autres circonſtances,
quelquesfois ceſte peine de glaiue, & de mort naturel-
le, a eſté reſtrainte & moderée à banniſſement, ou au-
tre mort ciuile {k}. Comme auſſi en pareils termes,
nous liſons de la loy Cornelie, eſcrite contre les
meurtriers, par laquelle les homicides ſont punis de
mort {l}; & neantmoins pour raiſon des circonſtances
qui ſe preſentent quelquesfois, eſt impoſée vne plus
